The baseline builds with all ten dependency checkouts at their pinned revisions. The working manuscript now includes a Ricci-flow argument for a uniform recognition gap. The geometric construction of those transplants remains open.

The area proof identifies the induced round metric’s measure with Euclidean cone measure, which is the missing link needed to use that constant in the indexed-height formula. I’m checking their composition with the sheet calculation now.

The checkout disconnected during integration. The named modules for the normal, round area, Sard, cap test transfer, and endpoint charge transfer had already built. I’ll check whether the current working tree is available elsewhere before reporting which public checks and blueprint builds are still pending.

Each side has its own surcharge \(2\sqrt{s}\,\beta+\beta^2\), including the full exterior comparison. At \(I=T\), the physical spectral deficit, modified constant test, and conformal spectral transport imply that a set of vanishing modified volume carries vanishing combined **physical** chiral charge. The positive-Ricci metric supplies the disk-containing balls. **The remaining endpoint issue is the derivative cost on the selected collars.** The shrinking-trim argument elaborated for finite disk families of unrestricted cardinality. It makes their total raw physical charge small. Narrowing those same collars can increase the straightening cost, and no strict saving below the \(2\pi\) allowance was established. No finite attaining metric, joint repair, or marked surgery cancellation was obtained. The manuscript’s newer uniform recognition-gap argument also has separate Ricci-flow and compactness dependencies.

I’ll check which edits survived the disconnect, then replay the geometric and intrinsic proofs against the current checkout. I’ll verify the final theorem types through `import SmoothPoincare` before updating the registers and rebuilding both blueprint formats.

The density replay and ordered principal-frame construction passed. Lean also checked that almost every ordinary round direction gives a Morse height on the same immersion. On the intrinsic side, E58 now bounds each omitted chiral charge on the same selected region. The collar theorem keeps the repair allowance on the widths it actually selects.

The openness proof passed using the three tests you proposed. A separate proof of Weyl-density continuity also removed the last regularity assumptions from the inclusive threshold theorem. Lean now produces an actual Morse height with at most one index-two point when the induced energy is at most \(64\pi^2/9\). HEAD advanced during the run, so I’m checking the final source digests against both the intake and the new revision.

The public build passed. All 367 inventoried Edition 03 declarations and all 293 declarations cited by the blueprint passed type and axiom checks. The rebuilt PDF and web chapter now include the inclusive Morse-height theorem and the E58 result that puts both raw exterior energies below \(T\) when \(I<5T/4\) and the supplied family meets one fixed volume tolerance.

**Lean now proves that an oriented isometric hypersurface immersion with induced energy \(E_+\le 64\pi^2/9\) has a Morse height with at most one index-two critical point**, under the compact-source hypotheses. This includes equality and requires no Yamabe sign or topological count floor. Smooth recognition from that height still requires the marked zero- or one-handle reduction and its boundary gluings. [Integrated proof](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/SmoothPoincare/Heights/OrientedIndexedMean.lean)

The density and principal-frame replays passed. The immersion supplies its own oriented normal, ordered pointwise frames and conull Morse directions. Positive determinant and two fixed quadratic evaluations of opposite sign prove openness of the middle locus \(U\) in one normal chart. For ordinary round probability, the verified mean is
\[
\mathbb E[m_2]=\frac{2}{8\pi^2/3}\int_U|\det A|\,dV_g,
\]
with multiplicity counted on the source. Under the separate topological floor of two, \(E_+<8\pi^2\) gives probability strictly above \(3/4\) of a Morse height with exactly two middle points.

On the intrinsic route, the marked-side constructor and corrected endpoint theorem passed. The \(2\pi\) lower allowance applies to repairs tested on **exactly the widths selected by the proof**. E58 bounds both physical chiral charges on the same exterior. For \(e_i\to I<5T/4\), one fixed omitted-volume tolerance puts both raw exterior energies below \(T=4\pi^2\) on a qualifying supplied family. Constructing the marked disks and paying the cutoff cost of a positive repair remain open.
